newsitem.title: USA: Forty-five charged in securities case.
newsitem.headline: Forty-five charged in securities case.

text.p: The Manhattan U.S. Attorney's office said Thursday it would announce securities fraud charges against 45 individuals following an investigation of illegal payments to stock brokers in connection with sales of over-the counter and Nasdaq stocks.
Officials from the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Federal Bureau of Investigation will be involved in the 2:30 p.m. EDT news conference, prosecutors said.
No other details were immediately available.
On Sept. 27, the SEC sued stock promoter Atlantic Capital Corp. of Orlando, Fla., and seven stock brokers for a scheme in which the brokers allegedly were bribed to recommend certain stocks.
The civil suit, filed in federal court in Orlando, alleged that the promoter netted about $2.6 million from the scheme.
A lawyer with the SEC would not comment as to whether Thursday's case involved the Atlantic Capital proceeding.
